verdict.rationale: Supermemory documents two pieces of this story. Container tags act as hard, isolated namespaces, which can keep per-user memory private. Its MCP layer and spaces offer a shared, authorized team memory context across assistants. It does not document how to selectively share specific memories between private and shared scopes, how to query across a user tag plus a team tag, or any per-memory permissions. Missing for 10: selective sharing of individual memories, cross-scope (private + shared) retrieval, documented access controls/ACLs for group memory, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can share selected memory across multiple agents or users (team or group memory) while keeping private memory private

citations.quote: A container tag is a hard boundary — its own namespace. Memories in one tag are never returned by a search scoped to another tag.
every memory tagged with `user_alex` lives in its own isolated space, completely separate from memories tagged `user_jordan`
Supermemory MCP gives every MCP-compatible assistant a shared memory layer, so technical and non-technical teams can collaborate with AI using the same authorized context.
A space keeps a team's documents, memories, and profile context focused, so AI retrieves the right knowledge without mixing unrelated work.
